title: Would You Drive 446 km Across China's Taklamakan Desert? | China Travel Expert
description:
Would you drive 446 km across a desert with no town, no farm, and no water?

That's the Tarim Desert Highway, cutting straight across the Taklamakan — the world's second-largest shifting-sand desert, about 337,000 km², nearly the size of Germany. For roughly 446 km the road runs through uninhabited dunes with no village, farm, or natural water source. The only people out there live in small well-houses spaced about every 4 km, pumping groundwater to keep a green shelterbelt alive so the sand doesn't bury the road. It opened in 1995.

🧭 Expert Tip: Fuel up and stock water at Luntai (the north end) before you start — the crossing takes hours and there's nowhere to resupply in between.

446公里横穿塔克拉玛干，一路没有村庄、农田和水源。
